uncited: It builds on [MPI Volume Rendering (1D/2D Decomposition)](2249-mpi-volume-rendering-1d-2d-decomposition.md) by introducing a graph-partitioning-based remapping step that adapts the static data distribution to the view.
The Clustering phase is a view-independent preprocessing step performed once.
*   Volumetric dataset $V$ (unstructured grid, e.g., tetrahedral cells).
*   Total number of clusters $a$ (empirically determined).
*   Viewing parameters (camera position, direction, etc.).
*   Node Weight: Proportional to cell volume (in World Space Coordinates, WSC).
*   Edge Weight: Proportional to the area of the shared face (in WSC).
*   Represents the initial distribution of $V$ among $K$ processors from the simulation phase.
*   Each cluster $C_i$ has a unique global identifier.
*   Identify clusters whose new mappings differ from their current mappings.
*   **Global Clustering Overhead:** Constructing the global view-independent visualization graph $Q_v$ for global clustering may be very expensive.
*   **Time Complexity:** The clustering phase is executed once, providing a preprocessing cost.
The remapping, local rendering, and pixel merging phases are executed for each visualization instance.
The complexity of remapping depends on the graph partitioning cost (MeTiS/RM-MeTiS).
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the visualization graph, simulation graph, cluster data, and remapping graph.
The use of local clustering reduces the memory overhead compared to global clustering.
Local clustering reduces preprocessing overhead.
The specific view-dependent weighting formulas are not detailed.
*   **When to use:** Suitable for parallel volume rendering on distributed memory systems where the viewing parameters change frequently, and dynamic load balancing is beneficial.
*   **When not to use:** If the viewing parameters are static, the remapping overhead may not be justified.
If the preprocessing cost is prohibitive, global clustering might be considered (though it has higher overhead).
The work models the OS decomposition problem for OS-parallel DVR as a Graph Partitioning (GP) problem with correct view-dependent node and edge weighting.
The proposed model generates a remapping graph by node and edge augmentations to the graph representing the computational structure of the parallel application.
A MeTiS-based remapping tool, RM-MeTiS, was developed by modifying and enhancing the original MeTiS package.
